_comment: How services/verb_reader.py reads a typed verb back into sarf's table. It builds the table once for each stand-in root below, turns every word in it into a shape whose stand-in letters are blanks, and matches the typed word against those shapes; the root a shape gives is then conjugated for real, so the table stays the only judge.
_placeholders: The letters that stand for the root in the stand-ins, first root letter first. No rule in ilal.json names any of them, and none is ever part of a prefix or an ending, so a stand-in's table is every sound root's table with other letters.
_stand-ins: One root of each kind the rules shape (conjugation.conjugates): sound, hollow by و and ي, weak-ended by و and ي, و- and ي-first, doubled, two weak letters apart, the hamza in each place, and a last letter that is also an ending's first (ثَبَتُّ، سَكَنَّا). Their weak letters and hamzas are real letters, kept in the shape.
_from-rules: Rules in ilal.json that act on named letters or roots: each gives more stand-ins, built only in the forms the rule itself lists. `letters` is the rule's key holding the letters and `into` where they go (_ is the letter; "first" puts it first in every stand-in above that opens with a blank, so اِدَّعَى is read as well as اِدَّخَلَ); `roots` names a key that lists whole roots.
_columns: Which table columns are read, and the name each is read as. `nahy` is لَا + the jussive, so its last word is the jussive itself. The command column of a person not spoken to is لِ + the jussive and adds nothing, so only the spoken-to rows (`addressed`) are read as commands.
_camel: Each column read as the dictionary's own features (asp: p past, i present, c command; vox: a active, p passive), for a verb only the table knows (verb_reader.reading_of).
_spellings: Spellings the book also allows that the table does not print. In Forms V and VI a present verb starting تَتَ may drop one of its two ت (تَنَزَّلُ for تَتَنَزَّلُ, لا تَحَاسَدُوا).
